experiment: VT-BSim seed-propagation densification for scattered RB3-specific game-TU identification
one_line: VT seed propagation does NOT densify per-TU clusters and DEGRADES precision vs a plain BSim query; neither method recovers the BinDiff-BSim 95% regime. No scattered game TU reaches the GO bar (>=8 newly-located real-bodied fns at >=90% precision).

stage0_mechanism.finding: The fork's BSim correlator is a Version-Tracking PROGRAM-CORRELATOR, not an H2-DB query. It computes feature vectors IN-SESSION via the decompiler for BOTH programs, reads ACCEPTED VTAssociations as seeds (findAcceptedSeeds), and extends along the call graph (Children/Parents round 0; GrandChildren/Siblings/Spouses/GrandParents round 1; plus single-parent hole-patching).
stage0_mechanism.cross_arch_ok: getWeightsFile(PowerPC:BE:64:A2ALT-32addr, PowerPC:BE:32:Gekko_Broadway) returns lshweights_nosize.xml (different sizes, both in {32,64}) -> the correlator RUNS cross-architecture using the size-independent (nosize) weights. Not a blocker.
stage0_mechanism.driver: tools/ghidra/VTSeedPropDriver.java (new VTSessionDB(src=Wii, dst=RB3Xenon); add seeds as ACCEPTED manual matches; BSimProgramCorrelatorFactory with USE_ACCEPTED_MATCHES_AS_SEEDS=true; correlate; export all matches).

setup.source_program: band_r_wii.elf-781439 (rb3-Wii dev decomp, MWCC PPC, NAMED functions; 36343 fns / 23729 real-bodied)
setup.dest_program: default.xex / RB3Xenon (retail XEX, MSVC VMX128, anonymous fn_8...; 35460 fns / 23185 real-bodied)
setup.seeds: 150 high-confidence Wii<->Xenon anchors from unified_id_rb3wii.json (conf>=0.85 & sim>=0.70 & size>=32) UNION crossval agree-fns; 146 applied as ACCEPTED (4 dest fns missing)
setup.isolation: Both shared MCP-locked projects left untouched. Worked on reflinked btrfs copies under /home/free/tmp/bsim_seed_work; Wii program exported to gzf and imported into the RB3Xenon project copy.

cross_tool_precision_vs_bindiff_ground_t.method: non-seed propagated matches whose Xenon VA is ALSO covered by BinDiff(conf>=0.9); agree if same Wii class or same normalized name
cross_tool_precision_vs_bindiff_ground_t.note: high-sim verifiable subsets are statistically thin (n=3..41) because propagated NEW matches rarely land on VAs BinDiff opined on; broad-threshold (oracle conf>=0.7) gave n=55..203 and the SAME ~18-24% precision
cross_tool_precision_vs_bindiff_ground_t.interpretation: Both are far below the prior BinDiff-INTERSECT-BSim 95%. Disagreements are real errors: _restgpr_23/25/26 compiler stubs propagated onto unrelated fns; BandCharacter::StartLoadClips mapped where BinDiff says DirectInstrument::NoteOff; many cross-class mismatches.

densification_per_stem.metric: NEW (non-seed) located real-bodied (>44B) fns at sim>=0.90, non-Quazal game stems, stem derived from Wii class->source map
densification_per_stem.key_finding: Seed propagation produced LESS dense per-stem clusters than the plain query, AND those clusters are still low-precision. Propagation did NOT turn singletons into clusters. The plain query is denser but ~40%-precision contaminated -> its dense clusters are unusable without an intersection filter.

go_no_go.bar: >=1 scattered game TU with >=8 newly-located unpinned real-bodied fns at >=90% calibrated precision, materially exceeding the 57 the plain crossval already gives
reasons: 0 game stems reach >=8 (or even >=5) newly-located fns under propagation
propagation DEGRADES precision relative to the plain baseline (call-graph extension drags in wrong neighbors)
the densest treatment GAME cluster is 3-4 fns and itself error-prone

calibration_caveat_important.finding: splits.txt .text-range stem-equality is INVALID as a precision oracle for SCATTERED game TUs.
calibration_caveat_important.evidence: Known-correct seeds fail it: GemTrainerPanel::GemTrainerPanel() (a conf>=0.85 BinDiff pair) sits at Xenon 0x82266818, INSIDE the CharBonesMeshes pin [0x82265608,0x82266ce0). GemTrainerPanel is unpinned/scattered and physically interleaved into another TU's carved span. 39/40 seeds-in-pinned-ranges 'failed' the range test -> the test is wrong, not the seeds. This is the ICF-scatter wall itself. Precision must be measured against the independent BinDiff oracle, NOT pinned ranges.

what_would_change_it: An INTERSECTION gate (BinDiff(conf>=0.7) AND BSim/VT-prop AND a third independent signal e.g. string/callee fingerprint) restores ~95% precision but the prior experiment already showed that only yields ~146 fns binary-wide, mostly singletons -- propagation does not add recall to that intersection.

A HIGH-CONFIDENCE LOCATOR that fuses multiple signals (BinDiff + string/callee fingerprint + Ghidra BSim + size/CFG) BEFORE per-method reconstruction -- the standing reframe in the roadmap (fuzzy-locator-reconstruction-design.md). VT seed propagation is NOT that locator: it trades precision for a small, noisy recall bump.

Better seeds: the 150 anchors are sparse and scattered (110 stems, mostly singletons), so the call graph offers little dense local structure to propagate through. A locator producing many correct same-TU anchors first could give propagation real clusters to extend -- but that is circular (you need the locator the experiment was meant to provide).
